description: From stone to a thought a machine can hold: refinement, crystals, patterning, switches, memory, and the processor that runs it all.

concepts.title: Silicon
concepts.summary: Ordinary stone, refined until almost nothing is left but silicon. Each step removes a little more chance: purify, grow the crystal, slice, pattern, layer. What comes out is rock that can hold a thought for a machine.

concepts.title: Stone
concepts.summary: Quartz sand and rock: silicon and oxygen, tangled together and common enough to walk on. Nothing here suggests a computer. That is the point.

concepts.title: Refinement
concepts.summary: Heat and chemistry strip away the oxygen, then impurity after impurity, until the silicon is purer than almost anything else people make: fewer than one foreign atom in a billion.

concepts.title: Crystal Ingot
concepts.summary: Molten silicon is touched with a seed crystal and drawn slowly upward. Atom by atom, the melt copies the seed's pattern, and one flawless crystal grows into a long cylinder.

concepts.title: Wafers
concepts.summary: The ingot is sliced into thin discs and polished flatter and smoother than any mirror you own. Each wafer is a blank stage waiting for billions of tiny structures.

concepts.title: Lithography
concepts.summary: Light is projected through a mask onto a coated wafer, printing a pattern finer than the light seems to allow. Deposit, expose, etch, repeat: hundreds of steps, layer over layer.

concepts.title: Transistors
concepts.summary: A switch with no moving parts. A small voltage decides whether current may pass. Billions of them, some only tens of atoms across, agree on zeros and ones.

concepts.title: Memory Cell
concepts.summary: One transistor guarding one tiny capacitor. Charge means one; no charge means zero. The charge leaks away, so the cell has to be reminded again and again.

concepts.title: RAM
concepts.summary: Billions of those cells laid out in a grid, refreshed many times every second. It forgets the moment the power goes, which is exactly why it feels so alive while it lasts.

concepts.title: Semiconductors
concepts.summary: Materials that sit between conductors and insulators, and whose behavior you can tune. That in-between nature is what lets a tiny signal switch a large current on and off.

concepts.title: Doping
concepts.summary: Add a few foreign atoms to pure silicon, one in millions, and it becomes a good carrier of extra electrons or of missing ones. Where the two kinds meet, a diode or transistor is born.

concepts.title: Band Gap
concepts.summary: The energy an electron must gain to start carrying current. Quantum mechanics sets it, and its size decides whether a material is a metal, a semiconductor, or an insulator.

concepts.title: Integrated Circuits
concepts.summary: Instead of wiring separate parts together, build all of them, and their connections, in one piece of silicon. It turned rooms of electronics into something the size of a fingernail.

concepts.title: Moore's Law
concepts.summary: The observation that the number of transistors on a chip roughly doubles every couple of years. It was more a target than a law, and it has been slowing as parts approach the size of atoms.

concepts.title: Processor
concepts.summary: The part that follows instructions: fetch one, decode it, do it, move on, billions of times a second. All of software is ultimately a very long list of tiny steps like these.

concepts.title: Binary
concepts.summary: Numbers written with two symbols. It suits hardware, since a switch is either on or off, and any information at all can be encoded as a long enough string of them.

concepts.title: Clock Rate
concepts.summary: A processor's metronome: a signal that ticks billions of times a second so every part moves in step. Faster ticks mean more work per second, and also more heat.
